newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Demand drives India gains, ITC leads run.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Demand drives India gains, ITC leads run.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished firmer again on Monday following local market gains and as prices were squeezed higher amid a shortage of stock, traders said.
They said a run in ITC was sparked by expectations of a good set of annual results on Tuesday and gains in TELCO came amid talk of a possible bonus issue from the truck maker.
"We have seen buyers across the board and prices are up on a short squeeze," a trader said, adding that local market prices would have to rise to justify current GDR levels.
Volumes were relatively thin, and a trader said there was concern in India that the key Bombay share index would struggle to break 3,800. It closed Monday up 18.67 points at 3,778.31.
"GDRs have gapped up. I think they are looking a bit expensive," the trader said.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.50 points up at 80.28, with the premium over the local market at 22.05 percent from 20.61 percent.
SBI picked up 52 cents to $24.50/25.50, ITC added 91 cents to $15.25/16.25 following gains in Bombay and TELCO was 32 cents better at $12.00/13.00.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index lost 3.33 points, or 2.81 percent, to 115.27, representing a discount to the local market of 3.41 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index added 1.32 points to 66.20 points, a premium of 36.78 percent over the local market.
